title: Upper friction zero
description: Essential: The student must state that the frictional force on the upper surface of block B is zero.

title: Lower friction equals F1
description: Essential: The student must correctly give the frictional force on the lower surface of block B as 16 N.

title: Correct friction coefficient
description: Essential: The student must calculate the coefficient of kinetic friction as 0.2.

title: Correct elastic force
description: Essential: The student must calculate the elastic force exerted by A on B in part (3) as 8 N.

title: Equilibrium reasoning for part (1)
description: Important: The student should apply Newton's first law or force equilibrium to relate the applied force to the lower friction.

title: Normal force calculation
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the total normal force from the table for part (2).

title: Free-body diagram for part (3)
description: Optional: The student may draw or describe a correct free-body diagram for block B in the second scenario.

title: Units in final answers
description: Optional: The student includes correct units (N, no unit for coefficient) with their numerical answers.

title: Confusing static and kinetic friction
description: Pitfall: The student incorrectly assumes non-zero friction between blocks A and B in part (1).

title: Incorrect normal force for part (3)
description: Pitfall: The student uses the total weight instead of just block B's weight when finding the friction on B in part (3).
